branch: NO BRANCH FIRES. A3 = 30/210 = 0.1429 with only 2 of 7 classes predicted (205 'cubic'), which equals the cubic base rate exactly — PREDICTION COLLAPSE, so the accuracy is not a reasoning measurement.

correct_reference_for_A3.why: A4 is the weak model's ceiling with PERFECT geometry, so A2 (0.7333) overstates the shortfall. Named in the pre-registration before the run.

emitted_position_quality.interpretation: the strong model emits syntactically perfect coordinate lists — correct elements, 5-decimal precision, median 48 atoms — and on half the structures NOT ONE lands within tolerance of a real atom. It generates the FORM of an extraction without the content.

atoms_emitted_distribution.note: computed over all 206 structures with an emitted list. An earlier prose figure of 45 came from a 43-record diagnostic on a CLASS-ORDERED PREFIX that was already discarded for the accuracy number; it leaked into prose while the numeric field was correct.

gates.conclusion: all gates pass, so the failure is the model's extraction rather than a harness artefact

what_is_supported: model-emitted structured extractions can be entirely fabricated while syntactically perfect, and downstream accuracy alone would NOT reveal it — 0.1429 could have been read as 'the weak model reasons badly'. Only scoring the intermediate against exact ground truth exposes it. This is a direct argument for the paper's instrument.
what_is_not_supported: any claim about whether the strong/weak difference is perception. The design premise failed, not the hypothesis: A3 can only test transplant if the transplanted content is perception.
own_reading_defect: at 43/210 I observed 0 correct; the executor submits in file order and eval.jsonl is ORDERED BY CRYSTAL SYSTEM, so that prefix was all triclinic/monoclinic. The documented prefix-slice defect, recurring. The partial number was meaningless.
limits: one strong model, one weak model, one sample, one handoff format. A different prompt might elicit real coordinates; this shows the obvious prompt does not.
